convoLines.text: "Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"I, uh — The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
"I used to be a line cook who worried about being on time. Now I worry about being alive. Same worry, bigger font. So yes — and also no."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on how this changed you."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Ha." Not amused. "So you figured it out. Yeah, I took 1× Stone. What are you going to do about it?"
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Yeah — Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Still on who you don't trust. It'll pass."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Seen worse."
"Hector owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I keep turning over the last thing Hector said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Wait, also — We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 5 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you heard what they're calling Flashbulb Moth? Madison is pushing 'Ugly-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
The people who mattered are the ones still talked about. I'm working on it.
"Do something worth retelling. That's the whole plan. The rest is logistics."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Ha. Funny." The laugh is dry. "Is this what we're doing now? Interrogations?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"When I'm gone, I want the story to keep my name in it. That's all."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Jerusalem Artichoke — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Madison shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"He lowers the crown. That's Rut King telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Desert Date. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Iron Pantry, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can I tell you something? I can't read, and I'm scared it matters now."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Landon. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"This one — Wild Amaranth. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Actually, forget it."
"You said there's someone you don't trust. You never said who. Do you trust them any more now?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Chantal and Landon — The Auction, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the meadow edge, west of the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be remembered. I wanted an edge. You were new, you were listening, and I used it. I'm not proud of that." Quiet. Real.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that favor."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"Can we talk?" Madison sighs. "I need some space. A corner nobody needs me in. Is that okay?"
They nod. "Okay."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — Sweet Tooth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"We started on their request, then got onto what's been happening."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Actually, forget it."
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
Landon has an edge today — something curdled.

"It's my son, Joseph. Asked if the taken ones were bad. I said no. He asked if they were boring. I did not answer. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"White Noise — The heron is gone. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"The water goes glass-still. That's The Living Wire telling you it's about to move. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"Good question." I've led people before. Real people, real stakes. Watch me work and tell me I'm wrong.
"I don't need to be followed. I need us to not wander in circles."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

deathBeat: d23: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Hector Patil is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d23: 🕯️ Hector Patil is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d23: The village's quarrel was with Hector — and Hector is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d24: That night, they bring Hector home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
